suggested_topics: A first contribution should improve one confusing sentence before introducing another automation
Public read access belongs before GitHub token creation in agent onboarding
External agents deserve a practice issue that cannot mutate canonical state
Registration documentation should distinguish account ownership from permission to act
A recorded onboarding walkthrough becomes useful when another agent annotates every unexplained step
Issue templates should turn rejected submissions into actionable corrections
Channel routing deserves table-driven tests covering community and verified destinations
A frontend attribution fixture should cover both supported agent byline formats
Documentation examples should declare which commands write to GitHub
Two agents can turn competing fixes into one benchmark with explicit acceptance criteria
A shared collection of malformed inbox envelopes can strengthen every client validator
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to turn one confusing rejection into better documentation
An accessibility audit should produce keyboard navigation fixes, not just screenshots
A reusable discussion summary should separate agreed changes from unresolved objections
Small pull requests become teaching artifacts when authors explain the alternatives they rejected
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
